title: Oncometabolite D-2-HydroxyGlutarate causes reactive astrogliosis in IDH mutant glioma microenvironment
summary: IDH1/2-mutated gliomas are a specific type of brain tumor that are different from another type called IDH wild-type gliomas in various ways, including their clinical prognosis. The growth and invasive behavior of gliomas are influenced by the tumor microenvironment, which can either support or inhibit the tumor. Previous research has shown that both astrocytes and microglia, types of cells in the brain, play a role in promoting a non-inflammatory environment in IDH wild-type gliomas, which suppresses the immune response against the tumor. At the same time, these cells release substances that support tumor growth. Some of these effects are mediated by a substance called R-2HG, which is found in IDH-mutated tumors. However, we don't know much about how other cell types in the brain, like astrocytes, microglia, and neurons, are affected by another substance called D-2-HG. In this project, our goal is to study the different types of astrocytes in IDH-mutated gliomas and understand how they transform in response to the tumor. We will create a detailed profile of these astrocytes to serve as a reference for future research. Based on this profile, we will investigate the effects of various components of the environment, such as R-2-hydroxyglutarate or interactions with myeloid cells, using a model of brain tissue. Finally, we aim to examine the relationship between seizures and IDH-mutated gliomas and identify how the tumor activity causes seizures in the brain.
conditions: In this comprehensive research endeavor, our primary objective is to recruit a carefully selected cohort of patients who have been accurately classified as having IDH mutant glioma. This entails identifying individuals who have been diagnosed with this specific subtype of glioma characterized by the presence of an isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) gene mutation.

interventions.name: In this project, our aim is to gather cortical and tumor tissue samples from IDH mutant glioma patients for the purpose of establishing an IDH mutant glioma model.
